title: Homotopy-pullback pasting criterion for spaces
statement:
Use spaces as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the path-space homotopy-pullback notion in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. For maps $r:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$, the path homotopy pullback is $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$, with all products and pullbacks formed degreewise; a specified commutation homotopy supplies the path coordinate of the comparison map. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccccc}A&\longrightarrow&C&\longrightarrow&D\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
A'&\longrightarrow&C'&\longrightarrow&D'\end{array}$$
be a diagram of spaces with commuting adjacent squares. If the right square is a homotopy pullback, then the left square is a homotopy pullback if and only if the outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback. In particular two adjacent homotopy-pullback squares paste to a homotopy pullback. The assertion also applies to specified homotopy-commuting squares: their comparison maps to the path pullbacks use the specified commutation homotopies, and the outer rectangle uses the concatenated homotopy.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.1.11 (Tag 0110, Transitivity), equation composite-homotopy-pullback. The specified-homotopy form uses the path-space model and the concatenated commutation homotopy. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this spaces formulation.

proof.text: Name the horizontal maps $a:A\to C$, $d:C\to D$, $h:A'\to C'$, $k:C'\to D'$, and the vertical maps $v:A\to A'$, $c:C\to C'$, $g:D\to D'$. Orient the specified square homotopies as $\alpha:ca\Rightarrow hv$ and $\eta:gd\Rightarrow kc$. Strict squares use the constant homotopies. We use the path model $P(U\to W\leftarrow V)$ from the statement, which is Kan by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. Here are the fibration facts needed below, derived from [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. For a Kan complex $W$, endpoint-pair evaluation $W^I\to W\times W$, $I=\Delta^1$, is a Kan fibration: a horn problem transposes to extension from $(I\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup(\partial I\times\Delta^n)$, an anodyne pushout-product. Evaluation at either one endpoint is a trivial fibration: a boundary problem transposes to $(I\times\partial\Delta^n)\cup(\{e\}\times\Delta^n)$, the pushout-product of the anodyne one-dimensional horn $\{e\}\hookrightarrow I$ with a boundary monomorphism. The cited boundary-lifting characterization includes $n=0$. Pullbacks and composites of Kan fibrations are Kan fibrations, by projecting, filling, and pairing a lifting problem. These arguments also apply when some spaces are empty. Horn inclusions are anodyne directly from their defining right lifting property for Kan fibrations and the definition of anodyne in [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Products of Kan complexes are Kan by coordinatewise horn filling. Transposition between maps into $W^I$ and maps out of a product with $I$ follows directly from the degreewise internal-Fun definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: 0110: path-model implementation of the fibrant replacements; endpoint lifting is Kerodon 00TM and 00UT.

proof.text:
Define the mapping-path replacement of $c$ and the right-square path pullback by
$$E=C\times_{c,C',\operatorname{ev}_0}(C')^I,\qquad p:E\to C',\quad (x,\lambda)\mapsto\lambda(1),$$
$$Q_0=D\times_{g,D',\operatorname{ev}_0}(D')^I\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D',k}C',\qquad q:Q_0\to C'.$$
An element of $E$ retains its free endpoint $b=\lambda(1)$. Step 1 makes $p$ and $q$ Kan fibrations: the maps $E\to C\times C\prime$ and $Q_0\to D\times C\prime$ are the pullbacks of endpoint-pair evaluation along $(x,b)\mapsto(c(x),b)$ and $(z,b)\mapsto(g(z),k(b))$, respectively. Compose with the projections to $C\prime$, which are Kan fibrations because $C$ and $D$ are Kan. Both total spaces are therefore Kan. The projection $E\to C$ is a pullback of single-endpoint evaluation and has all boundary lifts, so it is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Its constant-path section $j:C\to E$ is consequently a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three, and is a degreewise monomorphism because projection recovers $x$. The right-square comparison is
$$r:C\to Q_0,\qquad x\mapsto(d(x),\eta_x,c(x)).$$
It is a weak equivalence by the assumed homotopy-pullback property of that specified square.

source.place: 0110: replace the right square; explicit mapping-path replacement retains its specified commutation homotopy.

proof.text:
Construct a strict map $F:E\to Q_0$ over $C'$. For $(x,\lambda)\in E$, prescribe in $D'$ the two consecutive edges $\eta_x:gd(x)\to kc(x)$ and $k\lambda:kc(x)\to k(b)$. This is a simplicial map $E\times\Lambda_1^2\to D'$. On $j(C)\times\Delta^2$, prescribe the degenerate triangle $s_1\eta$: its edges $01,12,02$ are $\eta$, the constant edge, and $\eta$. The prescriptions agree on the intersection. The inclusion
$$(E\times\Lambda_1^2)\cup_{C\times\Lambda_1^2}(C\times\Delta^2)\hookrightarrow E\times\Delta^2$$
is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], applied to the monomorphism $j$ and the horn inclusion. Since $D'$ is Kan it has an extension $T$. Restrict $T$ to edge $02$ and put $F(x,\lambda)=(d(x),T_{02}(x,\lambda),b)$. This is a simplicial map, satisfies $qF=p$ exactly, and satisfies $Fj=r$ exactly by the prescribed degenerate triangles. Since $j$ and $r$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] proves that $F$ is a weak equivalence. The choice of $T$ is a filler of an explicitly specified lifting problem, not a presumed canonical operation concatenating interval paths.

source.place: 0110: replace the right square by an equivalent fibration over C′; triangle filling spells out composition of the specified homotopies.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] to the cospans $E\xrightarrow{p}C'\xleftarrow{h}A'$ and $Q_0\xrightarrow{q}C'\xleftarrow{h}A'$. Their comparison maps are $F,1_{C'},1_{A'}$, all weak equivalences, and $qF=p$ is the strict equation from Step 3. Both fibration hypotheses were proved in Step 2. It follows that
$$F_h:E\times_{C'}A'\longrightarrow Q_0\times_{C'}A'$$
is a weak equivalence. Degreewise, its source is exactly $P(C\xrightarrow{c}C'\xleftarrow{h}A')$; its target is exactly $P(D\xrightarrow{g}D'\xleftarrow{kh}A')$. Indeed a target simplex is $(z,\gamma,b,t)$ with $b=h(t)$ and endpoints $\gamma(0)=g(z)$, $\gamma(1)=k(b)$; delete $b$ and recover it as $h(t)$ for the inverse. These formulas commute with every simplicial operator.

source.place: 0110 proof final sentence: the same base change computes the left and outer tests; fibration invariance makes the replacement valid.

proof.text: The left-square comparison is $l:A\to E\times_{C'}A'$, $z\mapsto(a(z),\alpha_z,v(z))$. Under the identification in Step 4, $F_hl$ sends $z$ to $(da(z),T_{02}(a(z),\alpha_z),v(z))$. The triangle $T(a(z),\alpha_z)$ has edges $01=\eta_{a(z)}$ and $12=k\alpha_z$. Thus its edge $02$ represents exactly the concatenated outer commutation homotopy $gda\Rightarrow khv$. With this representative the outer comparison is $F_hl$. Since $F_h$ is a weak equivalence, the model-structure two-out-of-three axiom of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] says that $l$ is a weak equivalence if and only if the outer comparison is. By the path-pullback definition these are precisely the left and outer homotopy-pullback properties. Taking both adjacent squares to be homotopy pullbacks proves the pasting assertion.

source.place: 0110: both tests reduce to the same comparison; coordinate computation also treats the homotopy-commuting case.

proof.text: The result is independent of the triangle representative of concatenation. Given two maps $T_0,T_1:A\times\Delta^2\to D'$ extending the same consecutive edges $\eta a$ and $k\alpha$, prescribe them at the endpoints of a new interval $J=\Delta^1$, and prescribe the common horn map constantly along $J$. The inclusion of this prescribed domain into $A\times\Delta^2\times J$ is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $A\times\partial J\hookrightarrow A\times J$ with the anodyne horn inclusion $\Lambda_1^2\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$, after interchanging factors. By [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] it is anodyne; the Kan property of $D'$ supplies an extension. Its $02$ edge gives a simplicial homotopy, fixed at its two endpoints, between the two outer path coordinates. Together with the constant $D$ and $A'$ coordinates this gives a map $H:A\to M^J$, where $M=P(D\to D'\leftarrow A')$ is Kan by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], with $\operatorname{ev}_0 H=o_0$ and $\operatorname{ev}_1 H=o_1$, the two outer comparisons. Step 1 proves that both endpoint evaluations $M^J\to M$ are trivial fibrations and hence weak equivalences. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] gives $o_0$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $H$ is, if and only if $o_1$ is. Thus every triangle filler representing the concatenated homotopy gives the same test. Strict squares use constant $\alpha$ and $\eta$; then $l$ lands in $j(C)$, on which Step 3 prescribes the degenerate triangle, so the outer homotopy is constant as required. No independently chosen outer homotopy is substituted for the concatenation.

source.place: 0110 specified-homotopy extension: relative triangle filling and homotopy invariance make concatenation well-defined for the comparison test.
